content: Atidarsagene autotemcel is an autologous hematopoietic stem cell-based gene therapy specifically indicated for the treatment of children diagnosed with pre-symptomatic late infantile (PSLI), pre-symptomatic early juvenile (PSEJ), or early symptomatic early juvenile (ESEJ) forms of metachromatic leukodystrophy (MLD). This therapy is intended for autologous use only and is administered as a one-time, single-dose intravenous infusion. Before initiating conditioning therapy, it is essential to confirm the availability and proper storage of atidarsagene autotemcel. Additionally, a back-up collection of CD34+ cells must be secured to ensure treatment safety and efficacy. Interactions with Antiretroviral Therapy (ART): Antiretroviral medications (ARTs) may interfere with the manufacturing process of atidarsagene autotemcel. Patients should avoid taking ARTs for at least one month prior to cell mobilization or for the expected duration required for the elimination of these medications from the body. Vaccination Considerations: The safety and effectiveness of vaccinations administered during or following atidarsagene autotemcel treatment have not been studied. Vaccination is not recommended during the six weeks preceding the initiation of myeloablative conditioning and should be avoided until hematologic recovery is achieved post-treatment. If feasible, childhood vaccinations should be completed prior to the start of myeloablative conditioning. Specific Vaccines to Avoid or Use with Caution: 1. Live Vaccines (e.g., adenovirus types 4 and 7, BCG, dengue, chikungunya, Ebola Zaire): These vaccines should be avoided due to the lack of safety data during or after atidarsagene autotemcel treatment. 2. Inactivated or Adjuvanted Vaccines (e.g., hepatitis A, hepatitis B, influenza, COVID-19): These vaccines are also not recommended during the specified period around myeloablative conditioning. 3. Combination Vaccines (e.g., hepatitis A/B, human papillomavirus): These should be administered with caution and only if deemed necessary before conditioning. Influenza Vaccines: Quadrivalent influenza vaccines, whether adjuvanted, cell-cultured, or standard, should not be administered during the restricted period. If possible, these should be given prior to myeloablative conditioning. ART-Specific Medications to Avoid: Medications such as abacavir, atazanavir, bictegravir, cabotegravir, darunavir, dolutegravir, efavirenz, elvitegravir, emtricitabine, etravirine, fosamprenavir, indinavir, and others in the ART class should be avoided for at least one month before cell mobilization or until their elimination from the body is complete. These drugs may interfere with the production of atidarsagene autotemcel. In summary, careful planning and coordination are required to ensure the safe and effective administration of atidarsagene autotemcel. This includes avoiding specific medications and vaccines, completing necessary vaccinations beforehand, and ensuring the availability of back-up CD34+ cells.
